title: Foreign Languages Centre
main_content: Foreign Languages Centre Eight languages taught at different levels During your studies, you can improve your language skills in the subject-specific languages English, French, Russian, Spanish and German up to advanced level (CEFR C1/C2) or learn another foreign language. Arabic, Italian and Japanese are taught up to basic level (CEFR A1). HTW Berlin is one of the few universities in Germany with its own Foreign Languages Centre and offers language courses with subject-specific specialisations in the fields of business (B), technology (T) and design (D) as well as general language (G) in eight languages: B T D G Arabic • German as a foreign language • • • • English • • • • French • • Italian • Japanese • Russian • • Spanish • • In addition to the semester-long courses, intensive courses are offered which can be counted towards degrees if they conclude with an examination.

title: Re-registration
main_content: Re-registration Re-registration deadline You re-register for every semester. No e-mails or payment requests will be sent to you. If you do not re-register, you will lose your student status and will be de-registered. If the final oral exam (colloquium) is the only module that is missing to finish your studies, you should not re-register. Pay the semester fee : In order to re-register, transfer the semester fee to the bank account of HTW Berlin. Please note the applicable re-registration deadlines . Check your re-registration status and retrieve your enrolment certificate : You can check in the LSF portal whether your semester fee has been received and you are officially re-registered. Please note that proper re-registration can only take place if the health insurance contribution has been paid in full . Validate your student card : As soon as you are been re-registered for the new semester, you can update your student card at a card validation terminal. You can also retrieve enrolment certificates yourself from the LSF portal. Late re-registration Even if the regular re-registration deadline has expired, you still have four weeks to re-register. A late penalty fee is payable for late re-registration and this must be transferred without any additional request together with your semester fee to the bank account of HTW Berlin. Special Cases If you are completing your final semester and only have the final oral examination to do in the coming semester, you do not need to re-register (exception: Public und Nonprofit-Management). taking a dual study programme at two universities and are not exercising your membership rights at HTW Berlin, you should re-register at the other university and send proof of re-registration to Students Services. taking an external leave semester , please remember that you still need to re-register.

title: Dual enrolment
main_content: Dual enrolment Table of contents Taking two study programmes simultaneously Duel enrolment means taking two study programmes simultaneously in order to obtain two separate degree titles. You can take the two study programmes at the same university or study at two different universities in Berlin and Brandenburg. Before taking two study programmes simultaneously, you should think about this carefully — the average workload for a study programme at HTW Berlin is equivalent to a 40-hour work week. Conditions If you apply for two NC (restricted admission) study programmes at the same time and are granted admission to both, you can only choose one study programme. The option of dual enrolment is excluded in this case. If you are already enrolled on a study programme and apply for another NC (restricted admission) study programme, you will only be granted admission providing other applicants are not excluded as a result (Section 14 no. 2 of the Berlin Higher Education Act). Application Apply for your chosen study programme as normal to HTW Berlin by the application deadline. Only after you have been granted admission for the study programme can you then apply for dual enrolment. Documents for enrolment If you are enrolled at HTW Berlin and are re-registering for the new semester, submit the following documents by the respective deadlines: The Declaration regarding the exercise of membership rights [PDF] . You only pay the semester fee to the university where you will be exercising your membership rights. If you will not be exercising your membership rights at HTW Berlin, please provide proof that you have paid your semester fee at the other university. A current enrolment certificate for the other university. For dual enrolment on two Bachelor’s degree programmes: proof that the Bachelor’s study programme at the other university is not an NC (restricted admission) study programme.

title: De-registration
main_content: De-registration Table of contents De-registration at your request If you would like to interrupt or discontinue your studies, please contact the Student Advisory Service for advice first. Submit an application for de-registration (available in LSF ) by e-mail from your HTW account to the Student Services department . Retrospective de-registration is not possible. De-registration by request will be effective from your requested time: at the earliest upon receipt of the application at the latest with effect from the end of the current semester. An official de-registration certificate and a certificate for your pension scheme provider will be sent to you by Students Services department. Automatic de-registration You will be de-registered without request if you fail to re-register as required, e.g. if the required semester fee is not paid on time or is not paid in the full amount (not including late penalty fee) or you have not provided the necessary proof for your re-registration on time. do not pass modules and examinations or the final examination. pass your final examination (written thesis and oral examination). De-registration after successful graduation Have you passed your final exam? Congratulations! By passing the colloquium, you have successfully completed your studies at HTW Berlin. You will be de-registered on this date. The Examinations Office will inform you when you can collect your transcript of records and graduation documents, your official certificate of exmatriculation and a certificate for the pension insurance. This will take a few weeks. If you require immediate proof that you have ended your studies, please send your application for de-registration as well as your provisional certificate of completion and a photo of your cut but recognisable StudentCard to the Student Services Centre . The semester ticket is cancelled at the end of the month as the entitlement to use it expires. If you graduate before March/September, please send your application for a proportionate reimbursement and your provisional certificate of graduation to the Student Services Centre . Return the HTW StudentCard If you de-register, your status as a student will end and also your right to possess the HTW student card (HSC). Please make sure any remaining credit is paid out to you and then return your HSC to the Student Services department. A proof of destruction of the HSC by photograph of the HSC cut into pieces may also be accepted. The owner of the destroyed HSC should still be visible. Please attach this photograph to your e-mail with the application for de-registration. Reimbursement of overpaid contributions In case of de-registration before the beginning of the respective semester, you can apply for a reimbursement of the semester fee minus an administrative fee of 50 euros. In case of de-registration after the beginning of the respective semester, you can apply for a proportionate reimbursement of the semester ticket fee . Please note If you de-register in the current semester, you are still entitled to take examinations even after you have de-registered. You can take examinations for the first time or repeat them. The repeatability period for modules and examinations will continue, as this semester will be counted as a repeat semester. The same applies for studies in the final semester (exception: Public und Nonprofit-Management). If you have submitted your final thesis in the current semester and you only have the final oral examination left to do in the following semester, you do not need to re-register for the following semester. Even if you have de-registered, you can still take the final oral examination. When you de-register, you are not long entitled to mandatory health insurance in the statutory health insurance system based on your student status. However, if you do not have any other form of health insurance, you are entitled to another month of cover from your statutory health insurance provider. After you have de-registered, please promptly contact your health insurance provider. If you receive the German state student grant or loan (BAföG), inform the relevant authority (the Amt für Ausbildungsförderung) immediately about your de-registration.

title: Exemption from Semester Ticket
main_content: Exemption from Semester Ticket The semesterticket is your ticket to use the public transportation and is valid all across Germany. The semester ticket is mandatory for all on-campus students at HTW Berlin. Exemptions are possible under special circumstances. Valid reasons severely disabled person's pass with token students who are ill or disabled and therefore cannot use public transport study-related stay for at least three consecutive months of the respective semester outside the area of validity of the Deutschlandsemesterticket ( e.g. internship semester, semester abroad or thesis semester) enrolment at two universities with the Deutschlandsemesterticket (please also refer to our information on dual enrolment ) De-registration after the beginning of the respective semester, e.g. due to successful graduation Unfortunately, students on ZbwS degree programmes, part-time students and holders of a company ticket or JobTicket can no longer be granted an exemption. The requirements for exemption from the semester ticket are regulated in the "Vertrag zum Erwerb des Deutschlandsemestertickets". For detailed information on reasons for exemption, please contact the AStA (General Student Committee) of HTW: asta@students-htw.de or find information here: www.students-htw.de/update-zum-deutschland-semesterticket/ Application You will find the request form in LSF . It is to be submitted via contact form or e-mail from your HTW account, together with the required proof. The documents to be submitted are explained in the attachment to the application form. If you successfully completed your degree, please submit the provisional certificate of completion from the day of the colloquium as proof. Devaluation of the semesterticket In case of exemption from the semester ticket your ticket will be devaluated at the end of the month and cannot be used anymore for the public tranportation.

title: HTW StudentCard
main_content: HTW StudentCard Table of contents Functions of the HTW StudentCard The HTW StudentCard functions as a Student ID card Mensa card with wallet/payment function Payment for printing and copying services Library card for the HTW Berlin From winter semester 2023/24, the card will no longer function as a semester ticket. You can find the link to the Deutschlandsemesterticket in LSF . Your personal StudentCard Before you start your study programme, a welcome email will be sent to your private email address. The email will contain the login details for your HTW account and information on how to obtain your StudentCard. Please note the following information: You need to issue your StudentCard yourself using one of the card issuing terminals on the Treskowallee campus , building A, in front of room 149 or on the Wilhelminenhof campus , building F, Foyer entrance F1. After it has been issued, take your StudentCard to a card validation terminal so the current semester and validity period can be printed on it. You will need to validate your card again at the beginning of each semester. Card validation terminals are located on both campuses of HTW Berlin . Next semester: As soon as you have successfully re-registered for the new semester, you can then validate your card before the start of the new semester. The old and new semester will then be printed on the back of the card. Replacement issue in case of defect and loss If your StudentCard is broken or has been lost, you can apply for a new card at the Student Service Center (SSC). This can be done via the SSC contact form or in person during opening hours. If you are responsible for the defect or the card has been lost, you will have to pay a fee for a replacement card (EC card required). You will receive a document from the SSC with a new QR code to create a new card. You will also need this document to transfer your Mensa credit. Please present this document at the HTW Mensa cash desk.

title: Denied re-registration
main_content: Denied re-registration Failure to re-register If you do not pay the semester fee at all or pay not enough or pay it after expiry of the extended deadline, you will be automatically de-registered at the end of the previous semester and receive the de-registration notice. Other reasons for denied re-registration Regardless whether you have paid your semester fee on time, you can be denied routine re-registration for a number of reasons, e.g. missing proof of health insurance missing parts of the pre-study internship failure to fulfil your conditions of admission failure to attend scheduled examination counselling missing language test If such reasons exist, you will be informed in the LSF portal. For re-registration the missing proof is to be submitted by the applicable deadline.

title: Financing your studies
main_content: Financing your studies At HTW Berlin, only the following semester fees are charged to those participating in degree programmes. However, it is wise to plan for the financing of living expenses during degree programmes, because students usually need at least 950 euros per month to support themselves financially . Many are financially supported by their parents during their studies, get a part-time job or apply for a BAföG study grant or a scholarship . The precise amount of money required to complete a degree programme depends on several cost factors. The largest proportion is usually accounted for by the accommodation , thus determining the budget available for the remaining expenses. Average monthly expenses Rent including additional costs 400-650 Euro Food 180-250 Euro Clothing variable Learning materials variable Health insurance 130 Euro Telephone, internet, radio and TV license fees 25-60 Euro Leisure, culture, sport variable

title: Prospective students
main_content: Our study programmes Degree programmes Bachelor & Master Advanced Master's programmes Study programmes for international professionals HTW Foundation Study preparation for international applicants Why study at HTW Berlin? Small groups : There are no large lectures at HTW Berlin. Learning takes place in groups with a maximum of 40 students. Practical relevance : Modern laboratories, an internship semester in every bachelor's programme and lecturers with professional experience ensure practical relevance. Lots of support : From maths bridge courses before your studies to career advice after graduation: at HTW Berlin you will receive all-round support. Good infrastructure : WLAN, computer pools and a well-equipped library offer the best study conditions. International campus : Language courses in eight foreign languages, semesters abroad at 150 partner universities and English-language degree programmes open up international perspectives. Application Find out all about admission requirements and application deadlines. We look forward to receiving your application !

title: Part-time study
main_content: Part-time study Degree programmes at HTW Berlin are generally full-time. However, circumstances may arise that prevent you from completing the full semester programme. You can then choose part-time enrolment, i.e. attend fewer courses per semester and thus extend the full-time degree programme. Part-time study makes it possible to combine study and work or study and family. In individual cases, part-time study can also be an alternative to full-time study for students with disabilities and chronic illnesses. Table of contents What exactly does “part-time study” mean? Periods of study that you complete part-time count towards the standard period of study. Part-time semesters count as full university semesters and half semesters. You pay the semester fee in full. Exemption from the semester ticket due to part-time study is not possible. Information on the reasons for exemption from the semester ticket can be found on the Students’ Union (AStA) website. What is the difference between a part-time degree programme and a part-time degree programme with an employment component? In the part-time programme, the number of courses is reduced, but the lecture times remain unaffected. In contrast, the lecture times of part-time degree programmes with an employment component are adapted to the students' working lives and tend to take place in the evenings or at weekends. However, a connection between work and study is not mandatory. How can you apply for a part-time study programme? First of all, inform yourselves about part-time study and its implications by consulting the student counselling service . They will also help you to decide whether this is the right decision for you and suits your personal situation. Please send the application form from the LSF by email from your HTW account to the Student Service Centre by the stipulated deadline . When applying for part-time study, it is unnecessary to state a reason. How long can you study part-time? If you no longer wish to study part-time, please send an email confirmation of your cancellation from your HTW account to the Student Service Centre by the stipulated deadline. You can also find the corresponding form in the LSF . How does the part-time study programme work? During the part-time programme, you put together your own study plan. If you have any questions about enrolment, please contact your faculty administration office. The existing teaching and support services are available for use during part-time studies. However, no entitlement to a special part-time study curriculum exists. Please contact the relevant student advisory service for your degree programme to discuss the timetable for your part-time studies. You can also complete the final semester on a part-time basis. However, part-time study has no effect on the length of time taken to complete examinations, especially theses. What are the implications of switching to part-time study? Switching to part-time study may have a significant impact on the financial benefits you receive from non-university organisations, including BAföG, child benefit and housing entitlements. There may also be consequences with regard to taxes, health insurance and other issues. Part-time students are not eligible for BAföG When the BAföG entitlement ceases, there is a basic entitlement to housing benefit. In special circumstances, part-time students may be able to receive citizen’s allowance if all other requirements are met. The compatibility of part-time study with scholarships and student loans must be clarified on an individual basis. Students with a “residence permit for study purposes” should contact the State Office for Immigration or Gernot Welschhoff (International Degree-Seeking Students) in advance. Please clarify the implications of part-time study for the specified benefits with the relevant office. The social counselling service at StudierendenWERK Berlin provides detailed and individual advice on issues relating to student finance and living expenses. Who can help? Individual advice on study orientation and study organisation: Student Advisory Service Applications and examination-related issues: s tudent management For questions about specific study planning in the context of the degree programme and your personal schedule: Student Advisory Service for your degree programme For students with disabilities: Disability representative of HTW Berlin Students who care for children or relatives: HTW Berlin Family Support Centre In case of administrative issues: Student Services International Degree-Seeking Students: Gernot Welschhoff Social benefits for students: Social Counselling Service of StudierendenWERK Berlin

title: Certificates
main_content: Certificates Table of contents Free-of-charge certificates in the LSF Students enrolled at HTW Berlin can print out the following verified certificates from the LSF free of charge: Grade transcript from the current and previous semesters Enrolment certificate Enrolment certificate in English Enrolment certificate stating start date of studies Enrolment certificate stating start date of studies in English Certificate listing all examinations Certificate of passed examinations only Grade transcript (English certificate listing all examinations) Certificates subject to charge HTW Berlin students can request certificates and replacement certificates for a fee via the Campus Management System LSF . In the form you can specify whether you would like to receive the documents by post or collect them from the Student Service Centre. The Student Service Centre can issue the following documents: Additional certificates and replacements Officially attested copies of your degree certificate and grade transcript Officially attested copy prepared for apostille certification HTW Berlin alumni should use the form for replacement certificates [PDF] . Please contact studierendenservice@htw-berlin.de or go to the Student Service Center in person during opening hours. Please always provide the original document. You are welcome to bring photocopies with you. You can pay with EC card directly in the Student Services Department. You are also welcome to use the contact form for your enquiries. Table of contents Application, Admission and Enrolement We take care of all aspects of the student life cycle: we check your application documents, carry out the admission procedures and are happy to help you start your studies at HTW Berlin. Student-Life-Cycle incl. Examinations Management After your successful enrolement at HTW Berlin, we continue to accompany you throughout your entire student life cycle and take care of possible applications for holiday semesters, part-time studying or exmatriculation as well as any notifications of change. We are also responsible for any examination-related issues such as: the final processing of accredited modules and examinations when changing study programme or university , examination registrations , repeatability of modules and examinations , grades and module certificates , degree certificates and grade transcripts, applications to complete the Bachelor’s or Master’s thesis , dealing with any uncertainties regarding accreditation of modules or deciding whether additional modules are required when changing universities/study programmes, students who wish to discontinue their studies or are behind with their study programme, automatic de-registration in the case of irrevocably failed modules or failure to fulfil the study programme requirements, issuing of duplicates and legalisation/officially attested copies of degree certificates and grade transcripts, preliminary attestation of degree certificates for use abroad. The Examination Board of your study programme is responsible for the following examination-related issues: The Examination Board is appointed by the faculty committee for each study programme and decides on the accreditation of modules and examinations , decides on appeals against assessments of modules and examinations on the basis of written justification, decides on potential disadvantage compensation, grants permission for students to write their final thesis, is responsible for approving changes to the thesis title or topic or the withdrawal of a topic and for the extension of the writing period for a final thesis .

title: De-registration
main_content: De-registration Table of contents De-registration at your request If you would like to interrupt or discontinue your studies, please contact the Student Advisory Service for advice first. Submit an application for de-registration (available in LSF ) by e-mail from your HTW account to the Student Services department . Retrospective de-registration is not possible. De-registration by request will be effective from your requested time: at the earliest upon receipt of the application at the latest with effect from the end of the current semester. An official de-registration certificate and a certificate for your pension scheme provider will be sent to you by Students Services department. Automatic de-registration You will be de-registered without request if you fail to re-register as required, e.g. if the required semester fee is not paid on time or is not paid in the full amount (not including late penalty fee) or you have not provided the necessary proof for your re-registration on time. do not pass modules and examinations or the final examination. pass your final examination (written thesis and oral examination). De-registration after successful graduation Have you passed your final exam? Congratulations! By passing the colloquium, you have successfully completed your studies at HTW Berlin. You will be de-registered on this date. The Examinations Office will inform you when you can collect your transcript of records and graduation documents, your official certificate of exmatriculation and a certificate for the pension insurance. This will take a few weeks. If you require immediate proof that you have ended your studies, please send your application for de-registration as well as your provisional certificate of completion and a photo of your cut but recognisable StudentCard to the Student Services Centre . The semester ticket is cancelled at the end of the month as the entitlement to use it expires. If you graduate before March/September, please send your application for a proportionate reimbursement and your provisional certificate of graduation to the Student Services Centre . Return the HTW StudentCard If you de-register, your status as a student will end and also your right to possess the HTW student card (HSC). Please make sure any remaining credit is paid out to you and then return your HSC to the Student Services department. A proof of destruction of the HSC by photograph of the HSC cut into pieces may also be accepted. The owner of the destroyed HSC should still be visible. Please attach this photograph to your e-mail with the application for de-registration. Reimbursement of overpaid contributions In case of de-registration before the beginning of the respective semester, you can apply for a reimbursement of the semester fee minus an administrative fee of 50 euros. In case of de-registration after the beginning of the respective semester, you can apply for a proportionate reimbursement of the semester ticket fee . Please note If you de-register in the current semester, you are still entitled to take examinations even after you have de-registered. You can take examinations for the first time or repeat them. The repeatability period for modules and examinations will continue, as this semester will be counted as a repeat semester. The same applies for studies in the final semester (exception: Public und Nonprofit-Management). If you have submitted your final thesis in the current semester and you only have the final oral examination left to do in the following semester, you do not need to re-register for the following semester. Even if you have de-registered, you can still take the final oral examination. When you de-register, you are not long entitled to mandatory health insurance in the statutory health insurance system based on your student status. However, if you do not have any other form of health insurance, you are entitled to another month of cover from your statutory health insurance provider. After you have de-registered, please promptly contact your health insurance provider. If you receive the German state student grant or loan (BAföG), inform the relevant authority (the Amt für Ausbildungsförderung) immediately about your de-registration.
